text:
marco: anyone else seeing a sudden burst of retries against gpu inference svc? lots of 5xx and client retries since ~1938051200

rachel: I saw alerts — increased tail latency east-west between us-west-2a and us-west-2b :thinking:

marco: looking at metrics now, p95 for svc/redwood-gpu-infer jumped from 60ms -> 2s. Pod level shows repeated TCP resets.

kevin: ran `ipvsadm -Ln --statistics` on node-ep1, connections are all pinned to one endpoint even though we have 4 pods. snippet:
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Conns InPkts OutPkts
TCP  10.3.22.5:443 rr
  -> 10.1.5.12:8080               98321   98321   98290
  -> 10.1.6.22:8080               120     120     118
  -> 10.1.7.33:8080               45      45      44
```

nidhi: that smell like a hash imbalance. Did kube-proxy recently roll? kube-proxy logs show recent `--min-sync-period` bump on some nodes.

ana: also noticed MTU mismatch on the NICs: some nodes are on 9000 and others on 1500 after the recent host reprovision for the new GPU type. Could cause packet fragmentation/rdma fallbacks.

marco: good catch. RDMA fallback seen in dmesg on node-ep1: `mlx5_core transport fault, falling back to TCP` — that would change packet sizes and might interact poorly with IPVS hash distribution.

kevin: another datapoint: `kubectl get endpoints svc/redwood-gpu-infer -o wide` shows ep list but weights unknown. K8s service trafficPolicy is ClusterIP default. When I curl the VIP from within cluster traffic lands on node-ep1 95% of the time.

rachel: could be a combination: kube-proxy/IPVS hash + MTU-induced packet drops causing conn retry and IPVS sticky buckets not rotating.

marco: plan: 1) mark node-ep1 unsched for new pods and cordon, 2) drain to force re-distribution, 3) align MTU on reprovisioned hosts to 9000 or 1500 consistently, 4) toggle kube-proxy to `--ipvs-scheduler` round-robin for testing, 5) watch RDMA logs.

sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-204 - "svc skew + MTU mismatches causing retries". Pager duty notified.

nidhi: quick sanity check — does anyone recall if we enabled `net.ipv4.vs.conntrack` on these nodes? conntrack + IPVS can skew when conntrack entries become stale.

kevin: I verified on node-ep1: `sysctl net.ipv4.vs.conntrack = 1`. Conntrack table shows many ESTABLISHED entries pointing to pod 10.1.5.12. Clearing conntrack reduced immediate skew in a test.

ana: clearing conntrack on prod is risky but good for repro. Maybe we can rotate kube-proxy on a subset and test.

marco: actioned: cordoned node-ep1, starting drain now (will keep `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`). Next 10 mins monitor.

rachel: while draining, I'll push a small kube-proxy config change to force `ipvsScheduler=random` on a canary node and measure distribution.

kevin: also rolling a fix to provisioning templates to set MTU consistently (patch in infra repo ready).

marco: update: after drain started, connection distribution rebalanced within ~30s, error rate dropped 78%. RDMA errors still in dmesg for older hosts, ticket filed to replace firmware on those cards.

nidhi: follow-ups: add MTU check to node reprovision pipeline, add an alert for connection concentration (IPVS per-endpoint conn ratio > 10x), and document conntrack-ipvs interaction in runbook.

ana: copying findings to #incidents and will add kernel log examples. thanks all :thumbsup:
